title: Exponential change

review.interaction: implemented; numerical fixtures are not independent mathematical review

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematics. Applications and stories are original constructed scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical claims require claim-level sources before publication.
purpose: Track a quantity that changes by the same factor at every step.
meaning: Apply a scale factor to the current value again and again. The percentage stays the same while absolute change depends on the current size.

steps.expression: Round 614.4 to 614 px for a nearest-integer export.
steps.reason: Apply the stated final rounding policy after the ideal calculation.

result.exact: 614.4 px ideal; 614 px after final nearest-integer rounding

examples.interpretation: The retained fraction is 0.8³=0.512, or 51.2% of the starting width.

properties.claim: Each completed pass multiplies ideal width by the same factor.

prompts.prompt: Why does a 20% reduction remove fewer pixels later?
prompts.answer: The percentage applies to the current width, which is smaller after each pass.

prompts.prompt: Does 1.5 passes execute one and a half resizes?
prompts.answer: No. It shows the interpolation W₀qˣ between integer-pass results. Completed operations remain whole numbers.

definition.setting: Repeated positive scaling and its explicit real-exponent interpolation.

signature.W_0: positive initial image width in pixels
signature.q: positive dimensionless scale factor per pass

conditions: The initial width is positive and the same positive scale factor is applied at each completed pass.
Completed resize passes are nonnegative integers. Fractional inputs show declared geometric interpolation, not a fractionally executed operation.
The model tracks ideal width; a real raster image has integer dimensions and needs an explicit rounding policy.
definition.domain_notes: The interpolation W(x)=W₀qˣ is defined for real x≥0. Actual completed passes remain integers. The controls admit q=1 as the constant boundary case; a nonconstant exponential function has q≠1. Renderer bounds: width 1–2000 px, factor 0.25–2, pass coordinate 0–8.
definition.proof_status: Repeated multiplication yields the integer-step rule by induction; the real-exponent curve is an explicitly chosen interpolation.

grammar.pronunciation: W of n equals W zero times q to the power n
grammar.formation_rule: Raise the dimensionless factor to the pass count; multiply by initial width.
grammar.precedence: Evaluate qⁿ before multiplying by W₀. The expression (W₀q)ⁿ is different.

symbols.role: completed passes; fractions only for interpolation

scopes.domain_condition: W₀>0, q>0, n≥0; completed passes have integer n

parse_errors.reason: A negative factor does not give a real-valued scaling curve for all fractional inputs.
This cubes the starting width too; repeated resizing requires 1200 × 0.8³.

grammar.ast_coverage: The tree models the right-hand quantity. The output label, function declaration, physical assumptions and rounding conventions are explicit metadata.

interactive.description: Resize a photo frame by a repeated factor; integer markers show completed passes and a smooth geometric interpolation joins them.

controls.text_input_policy: Keep invalid input visible with an explicit error; never silently clamp or reuse a stale answer.

interactive.compute: output = initial * factor ** time. Internal time is the displayed pass coordinate n. Integer n gives ideal completed-pass widths; fractional n is geometric interpolation. Keep model output unrounded and state pixel rounding separately.
invariants: At zero passes, output equals initial width.
Consecutive completed-pass widths have ratio factor.
At factor one, output stays constant.
Fractional pass inputs are labeled as geometric interpolation, not completed operations.
limits: The controls define a finite illustrative window, not the full mathematical domain.
Shape size and accessible numeric output use the same validated parameters. Display interpolation is not an observation.
Invalid parameters produce an explicit failure, never a stale valid result.
The smooth curve between passes is a display convention. Real operations have integer counts and raster dimensions need rounding.
interactive.fallback: Read the formula, substituted values, worked steps and labeled output without animation.
